text:
devin: FYI -- autop-run flagged a sample-ratio drift on the session-token-routing-v2 canary at 5%. see telemetry: https://console/redwood/dashboards/exp/1245 :eyes:

maria: wait, drift how? traffic split was 5/95 for canary/control, that's weird. did routing sticky cookie kick in?

samir: early glance: ~72% mobile in canary, ~38% mobile in control. looks like client-side routing or UA-based sticky route.

devin: exact alert payload from rollout-bot:
```
rollout-bot: experiment=1245 metric=conversion sample_ratio_p=0.0002 sample_ratio_control=0.95 sample_ratio_variant=0.05 observed_variant_frac_mobile=0.72 observed_control_frac_mobile=0.38
```

nina: ugh. That explains the conversion bump. Not a treatment effect if segments are different. :face_with_raised_eyebrow:

henry: question: did we use simple Bernoulli assignment at edge? or a hash of session id that might be missing in mobile clients?

tara: config shows routingPolicy: cookie-first then fallthrough-to-ip-hash. mobile app might not set cookie, so falls back to IP-hash -> geographic skew.

samir: we should treat this as a sample-ratio-mismatch (SRM) not a positive signal. recommend pausing the ramp and run stratified checks.

devin: proposal: rollback ramp to 0% immediately, then re-run with enforced deterministic assignment server-side (server-assigned bucket) and stratify by client_type for analysis. Thoughts?

maria: agree pause. but quick mitigation: set canary->control pin to preserve user continuity until we fix assignment, otherwise we risk double-assigning users.

nina: product concern: if we pause, SLAs and team expectations need clarity. we should message support + customers in the canary cohort.

henry: ops note: pausing is cheap. I'll flip the rollout to hold state and add a marker event to the audit log.

samir: analytics plan (short): compute reweighted ATE using inverse probability weighting by observed assignment prop within strata (mobile/desktop). SQL: 
```
SELECT strata, sum(outcome / p_variant) / sum(1 / p_variant) - sum(outcome / p_control) / sum(1 / p_control) AS ipw_diff
FROM (
  SELECT client_type AS strata, user_id, outcome,
         CASE WHEN assigned='variant' THEN 0.05 ELSE 0.95 END AS p_variant,
         CASE WHEN assigned='control' THEN 0.95 ELSE 0.05 END AS p_control
  FROM experiments.exp_events
  WHERE experiment_id=1245 AND event_time < '2024-12-01'
) t
GROUP BY strata;
```

tara: also add a quick dashboard panel that shows sample_ratio_by_strata and assignment_entropy so we can alert early next time. I'll file a devex ticket.

devin: decision then: (1) hold canary at 0% ramp, (2) alert product + support, (3) re-run analysis with stratified IPW and post-hoc correction, (4) fix assignment to server-side deterministic bucket for next attempt, (5) add SRM guard to console that blocks ramps >1% if sample ratio differs >10% across primary strata.

maria: +1 on guard. also let's add a runbook snippet for SRM that suggests "do not stop immediately unless metric delta is > 3x expected and SLO impacted" — prevents knee-jerk halts.

nina: product ok with that runbook text. please include customer-facing note template.

rollout-bot: noted. created ticket RD-PLAT-8811 (pause-canary, add-audit-tag), RD-PLAT-8812 (assignment-fix-server-bucket), RD-PLAT-8813 (console-srm-guard).

henry: I'll tag the incidents channel and notify infra pager if we see any SLO blips in last 15m.

devin: thanks all. samir and tara, can you take 8812/8813? aim: hotfix in next 48h.

samir: taking 8812. will start with a small fast-path change: server assigns bucket at auth and returns header X-RD-BUCKET.

tara: taking 8813. will add UI flag + threshold config + telemetry panel.

maria: I'll draft the customer note and post in #support once ready.

devin: final check: we keep experiment data but mark pre-fix traffic as "non-randomized" for analysis. we'll publish a mitigation blurb in the experiment audit. :memo:
